- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–15% to avoid overreacting to bullish sentiment.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if 2+ consecutive days show negative sentiment.
- If recent price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of price decline after peak), reduce forecast momentum and add a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overextended trends.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of sentiment are neutral or mixed, apply a 2–4% downward correction to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- If forecast spikes after a sharp price drop (e.g., 10%+ drop in 3 days), reduce the spike magnitude by 10–20% to account for sentiment lag and market correction.
- When sentiment history shows repeated extremes (e.g., 2+ days of 1.0 or -0.3), apply a smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility — avoid abrupt directional shifts unless sentiment confirms it.
